newsitem.title: USA: Intermediate muni yields rise over week -- Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Intermediate muni yields rise over week -- Delphis.

text.p: Yields in the intermediate range of the municipal yield curve rose in the week ended Thursday, while most other yields held steady, Delphis Hanover Corp. said Friday.
Yields rose five basis points on ten-year Aaa-rated bonds, moving to 5.15 percent, but Baa-rated ten-years were unchanged at 5.95 percent.
Average yields on one-year municipal bonds rose five basis in the triple-A category, to 3.85 percent, and were unchanged for other investment-grade bonds.
The muni market was mostly in line with Treasury market trends for the period. The yield on the Treasury's 30-year bond gained four basis points on the week, moving to 7.11 percent.
Thirty-year municipal yields, meanwhile, were unchanged across the credit spectrum, holding at 5.80 percent for Aaa-rated bonds, and 6.65 percent for 30-year Baa's.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis were yielding 81.6 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday.
The municipal yield curve flattened five basis points in the triple-A category, leaving 195 basis points to separate one-year and 30-year munis.
The Baa yield curve between one-year and thirty-year bonds was unchanged at 200 basis points.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years narrowed five basis points to 80 basis points, and the 30-year spread was unchanged at 85 basis points.
